_headline: **Two stocks qualify as hard passes, both with caveats: Grand Canyon Education (LOPE) and Kanzhun (BZ).** NVIDIA (NVDA) clears every numeric gate but is excluded under the existential-news rule. Halozyme (HALO) fails one gate on a definitional choice and needs your decision. Stage 2 confirmation gates (three-scenario DCF: base-case upside >= 15%, worst-case downside <= 8%) have not been run, so these are screening-stage passes, not buy recommendations.
_result_note: Target upside, PEG and broker rating are the Zacks figures (the screen's designated provider); the EV/EBITDA percentile is the current multiple's rank within its own five-year history. With only two qualifiers the rank-normalised composite is coarse: each component is simply 100 for the better name and 0 for the other. An independent skeptic re-derived every gate for each of the three names from raw pages and filings; it confirmed both passes as 'hard pass with caveats' and upheld the NVDA exclusion.
_funnel: Supplied list: 30,000 global tickers; 5,294 are listed on the screen's exchanges (NASDAQ 2,387, NYSE 1,901, LSE 867, NYSE American/Arca 138, Cboe 1). Nine did not match the bulk data feed and were checked individually: none is an oversold candidate (CFR, ROKU, BWMN, PTLE and HWG have RSI between 53 and 77; ARI last traded 2026-11-06 at RSI 12; TCBI, ACHV and EMAN no longer return price data).
Market cap > $1B and 90-day average traded value > $10M: 2,186 names (2,065 US, 121 LSE; GBP converted at 1.3208 USD, 2026-11-13).
RSI(14) < 30 at the 2026-11-13 close: 36 names, all US-listed. No LSE name qualifies: the two oversold LSE names above $1B (Kainos, Coats) trade under $10M a day.
Regime: SPY closed 1.3% below its 50-day MA (754.37 vs 764.43), far from the 10% systemic-panic trigger, so the 25% fence is a hard exclusion.
Falling-knife fences: 13 names sit more than 25% below their 50-day MA and are excluded; none has RSI < 15. 23 remain.
Fundamental, valuation, sentiment and EV/EBITDA-history gates: 3 names clear all of them (NVDA, LOPE, BZ).
Existential-news exclusion and thesis filter: NVDA excluded; LOPE and BZ qualify.

Cross-checks: recomputing Wilder RSI from two independent price histories reproduced the provider RSI to within 0.05 on all 74 names with RSI < 33, so no name sits on the wrong side of 30. Finviz's own RSI < 30 screen contains all 36 names; its nine extras are five names that fail the $10M liquidity floor and four NYSE ADRs absent from the list (PBR, PBR.A, YPF, VIST), which were evaluated anyway and fail.

existential.summary: Decline is an earnings reaction: shares fell 18.9% on 2026-11-05 after Q3 results (revenue +2.4%, below the company's own guide; full-year guidance lowered and re-issued, not withdrawn). No fraud, restatement or going-concern language. One open item did not drive the fall but matters: see the first flag.

thesis.summary: Limb (c), growing demand: university-partner enrollments +5.2% to 145,270, online +7.1%, off-campus sites +12.6%, two new sites opened in 2026 (Q3 release, 8-K 2026-11-04). Growth slowed from +7.6% a quarter earlier, with no new partners. No exposure to the listed growth themes and no specific incentive.

LOPE.entry: the last new 20-session closing low was 2026-11-09, four sessions ago, so the stabilisation test (five clear sessions) is not yet met; wait for a fifth session without a close below $116.16. A later close below that level means the stop governs. The oversold window is narrow: a further gain of about 2% lifts RSI above 30.
flags: The CFO has been on paid administrative leave since 2026-08-21 'in connection with an ongoing governmental investigation involving a non-employee third party's trades in Company stock' (8-K filed 2026-08-24). The company says it is not a focus and that its financial statements and accounting are not at issue; the stock did not react at the time, and the Q3 statements were signed by an interim CFO. The investigation is unresolved.

The 3-year EPS CAGR is 10.4%, barely above the 10% floor (GAAP diluted EPS $5.73 in 2022 to $7.71 in 2025). It passes only because 2022 was a trough year and the share count fell 13%: net income grew 5.4% a year, and the two preceding three-year windows fail (9.3% and 7.7%).

The three analyst gates rest on thin coverage: 4 brokers for the rating (one Strong Buy moving to Hold would put it at exactly 2.00, a fail), 3 targets, 2 EPS estimates. The targets are fresh (Truist to $180 and Barrington $200 on 2026-11-05, BMO to $173 on 2026-11-06); Zacks' $187.33 average still carries BMO's old $182, and the refreshed mean of $184.33 is 52.8% above the price.
The 15% long-term growth rate behind the Zacks PEG is above anything the company has delivered (10.4% three-year EPS CAGR; Finviz carries 9.7%). The gate would still pass down to 8% growth.
Sentiment is poor: Zacks Rank 4 (Sell), four downward and no upward EPS revisions in 60 days, Zacks industry rank 160 of 247.
Concentration: Grand Canyon University is 96% of enrollments, and the amended services agreement in force since Q3 narrows the fee base to tuition and academic fees.
Balance sheet is net cash today, but liquidity fell $138M in nine months on buybacks, a $100M revolver was signed on 2026-09-28 to fund more, and the board added $355M of buyback authorisation.
No catalyst is near (next earnings expected 2027-02-17); three-year price return is -12.6% and the three-year Sharpe ratio is -0.08.

existential.summary: ADS fell 25.3% on 2026-11-12. Headlines attribute it to softening hiring demand, soft revenue guidance and insider selling; targeted searches found no fraud, restatement, withdrawn guidance or regulatory action. No company filing or release explains the move, so the trigger is known from headlines only.

thesis.summary: Limb (c), growing demand: Q2 2026 revenue +14.1%, paid enterprise customers +10.8% to 7.2M, monthly active users above 70M for the first time (6-K 2026-08-25). November headlines citing softening demand cut against this; Q3 results on 2026-11-25 will settle it. AI is a product feature here, not exposure to the listed themes.

BZ.entry: the 25% gap is one session old, so there is no stabilisation evidence; wait for five sessions without a close below $12.49, which runs into the 2026-11-25 results. The signal is one session wide: a close at or above $13.12 lifts RSI above 30, and a close below $11.82 trips the falling-knife fence.
flags: Event risk: Q3 results on 2026-11-25 arrive before any stabilisation can be confirmed, and a one-day 25% gap shows the stock cannot be relied on to honour an 8% stop.

Most analyst inputs pre-date the drop. The Zacks rating (1.29, 14 brokers) and the Zacks EPS consensus are unchanged for one to three months. Only three actions post-date it: Citi $26 to $22 (11-12), Barclays $20 to $17 (11-13) and an 86Research upgrade with a $17 target (11-13). Even $17 is 31% above the close, and a 15% cut to every target would still leave about 39% upside, so the gates hold, but on numbers that have not been reset.

Foreign private issuer reporting in RMB: SEC XBRL data is annual only, so TTM free cash flow, Altman Z and net cash come from providers (S&P via stockanalysis, FactSet, Zacks) rather than from filings. Market cap ranges from $4.9B to $6.1B across providers because of differing share counts.
The EV/EBITDA gate rests on an 18-quarter provider series (listed June 2021): SHORT SERIES, quarterly not monthly.

The 191% EPS CAGR is off a near-zero 2022 base (RMB 0.12 per share), and trailing GAAP earnings include a large non-operating gain, so the 9x trailing P/E overstates cheapness (about 11x on Zacks' non-GAAP EPS).

Insiders and a major holder have been sellers: the founder sold about $110M of shares on 2026-09-21, Finviz shows $122M of open-market sales and $381M of proposed sales in six months, and Tencent's stake was reported at 2.2% in a 13G/A filed 2026-11-10.
Three-year price return is -13.8% and the three-year Sharpe ratio is 0.09.

flags: Consensus is stale: about three quarters of the Zacks targets pre-date the resignation. The twelve targets issued 11-11 to 11-13 have a median of $187, only 14.8% above the price, which would fail the 15% upside gate.
The price is 1.1% above the falling-knife cutoff ($160.99) and traded through it intraday on 11-12 and 11-13.
Thirteen analyst downgrades between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (Finviz); the Zacks broker rating moved from 1.13 to 1.47 in a week.
Still printing new 20-session closing lows (four in the last five sessions); the 5.7x-volume flush on 2026-11-12 is one session old.
Earnings on 2026-11-17 will be reported under an interim CEO.
NVDA.exclusion_detail: **Why excluded.** The screen's rule removes names whose drawdown is driven by credible fraud allegations or by regulatory or legal action that plausibly reprices the business permanently, because trailing fundamentals cannot see such events. About half the fall from the October high was a sector selloff, which does not count. The company-specific leg does: securities class actions over disclosures (Reuters, 2026-11-10), a board investigation with outside counsel (CNBC, 2026-11-10), reported FBI and DOJ inquiries including a chip-diversion probe (NBC News 2026-11-10, Semafor 2026-11-12), a congressional subpoena threat (Bloomberg, 2026-11-11) and tougher China chip curbs described as likely (Reuters, 2026-11-12). Against exclusion: no restatement, going-concern language or withdrawn guidance has been reported, the DOJ has not confirmed the company is a target, and 40 of 53 Zacks brokers still rate it Strong Buy. This is a judgment call, and all of it except the 8-K rests on headlines rather than article text. On a narrow reading NVDA would clear every numeric gate on every provider and score 14 of 14 on the Tier-2 criteria, though its upside gate would fail on post-event targets alone. Revisit after the 2026-11-17 results.

_near_miss: **HALO (Halozyme) needs your decision.** It fails one gate, and only on how EBITDA is defined. Net debt is $2.18B. On as-reported EBITDA ($793M, which includes a $285M acquired-R&D write-off and a $49M impairment booked in Q4 2025) net debt/EBITDA is 2.74x, above the 2.5x limit, and the filing-based EV/EBITDA series also fails. On the providers' adjusted EBITDA ($1.14–1.15B, excluding those one-offs) the ratio is 1.9x and the EV/EBITDA gate passes (Option A, 12.0x against a 12.1x three-year average). Your prompt specifies as-reported EBITDA for the EV/EBITDA gate, so I have left it out. If you accept adjusted EBITDA it passes every numeric gate, narrowly on two of them: Zacks target upside is 15.1% against the 15% floor, and Zacks broker rating is 1.80 (Finviz 2.09). Its decline followed Q3 results on 2026-11-05 (guidance raised, but less than hoped) and a Morgan Stanley downgrade on 2026-11-11; recent demand evidence includes an FDA approval of a partner drug using its technology (2026-11-06) and an expanded argenx collaboration (2026-10-06). It has not had the full skeptic review the three names above received.

**Consolidation zone (notes, section 1).** Neither name has formed a base. For both, ATR and Bollinger-band width are at the top of their one-year range (volatility is expanding, not compressing), and LOPE's 50/100/200-day EMAs are spread across 8% of the price. BZ's EMAs are clustered within 2%, but the price has just gapped below all of them. A volume-profile reading needs intraday data, which was not collected.
_verification: Four separate agents checked the result after the screen ran. Three acted as skeptics, one per surviving name, re-reading every deciding figure on the raw Zacks, stockanalysis, Nasdaq and SEC pages and recomputing RSI, the 50-day average and the EV/EBITDA statistics. The fourth looked for names wrongly excluded.

- **LOPE: hard pass with caveats.** Every numeric gate confirmed; the EPS-growth, PEG, target and rating gates were marked fragile for the reasons in its flags. The skeptic found the CFO-leave filing that my first reading had missed.
- **BZ: hard pass with caveats.** Every numeric gate confirmed; PEG, target, rating and RSI were marked fragile because the inputs pre-date the drop and the RSI signal is one session wide.
- **NVDA: exclusion upheld**, as a judgment call.

- **No name was wrongly excluded.** All 14 near-miss names were re-read from raw sources; every Zacks rating, PEG and target parse matched the page. HALO was identified as the one name that turns on a definition.

- **Pipeline defects found and fixed before this report was regenerated:** filing-derived EBITDA omitted separately tagged intangible amortisation (HALO); the Zacks target page carries two snapshots and the staler one was being used; the EPS pair lagged a year for filers that have reported but not yet filed their annual report (DGII, FFIV, DOX); a Finviz PEG built on a trailing P/E could decide the forward-PEG gate when Zacks published none; IFRS filers' negative-signed D&A corrupted the filing-derived EBITDA (VIST). None of these changed which names pass.

- **Remaining known limits:** filing-based figures for September-year-end companies are a quarter older than providers' (DGII, FFIV); the EV/EBITDA history includes the current observation in its own averages; filing-based EV subtracts cash only, while the solvency test also subtracts short-term investments; dual-class issuers (GEF, TEAM) fall back to the provider EV/EBITDA series.
_method: - **Bulk first pass:** TradingView scanner (fundamentals and estimates supplied by FactSet) for every in-scope ticker: RSI, 50-day MA, market cap, traded value, and first-pass fundamentals.

- **Per-candidate verification of all 40 oversold names:** Zacks (PEG, broker rating, price target, rank, style scores, industry rank), stockanalysis.com (S&P Global Market Intelligence: Altman Z, FCF, debt, EBITDA, quarterly EV/EBITDA history), SEC EDGAR XBRL filings (FCF, EBITDA, debt, cash, shares, split-adjusted annual EPS), Nasdaq.com (daily prices, 13F position changes, analyst data), Finviz (snapshot, analyst actions, insider trades, news), FRED (3-month T-bill 4.14% on 2026-11-12) and Google News RSS headlines.

- **Gate decisions:** each gate is evaluated on every provider that reports it and decided by a stated hierarchy (filings first for FCF, solvency and EPS; Zacks first for PEG, target and broker rating; FactSet first for Altman Z). The evaluation file records every provider's value and flags disagreements.

- **EV/EBITDA history:** primary series is monthly and point-in-time, built from SEC filings (EBITDA = operating income + D&A over the trailing four quarters, debt and cash from the latest balance sheet public at each month-end) and month-end closes. The provider's 20-quarter series is the cross-check, and becomes primary for non-US filers and wherever the filing-derived EBITDA fails its quality check.
- **Technicals:** Wilder RSI(14) and the 50-day SMA are recomputed from two independent daily price histories (stockanalysis and Nasdaq, split-adjusted closes).

- **Substitutions:** no provider 'Profitability Score' or 'Solvency Score' is publicly retrievable, so the Tier-2 profitability criterion uses the Piotroski F-Score (flagged) and financials' Altman-Z substitute is reported as not evaluable. Interest coverage is EBIT over interest expense. Where Zacks, Nasdaq and stockanalysis publish no forward PEG, the gate is not evaluable.

- **Unavailable sources:** Yahoo Finance rate-limited this machine (HTTP 429), Macrotrends and Stockopedia answer with bot challenges, MSN serves its data through a keyed API, and FT Markets forecasts are subscriber-only. None was worked around. No LSE candidate reached the stage where the Stockopedia fallback would have been needed.
- **Judgment calls:** the thesis-filter and existential-news results are analyst judgments made from headlines and filings, not article text.
- **Not done:** Stage 2 (CAPM, three-scenario DCF, the base-case and worst-case confirmation gates) for either qualifier.

This is a rules-based screen on public data as of one date, not investment advice. Analyst targets and ratings lag sharp price moves, and a screening pass says nothing about whether the Stage 2 valuation gates would hold.
